This action will completely delete all files associated with MobileGlues. This includes:

• All configuration files: Any of your custom settings, preferences, and possible configuration files required for the application to run will be removed.
• Cache files: The GLSL cache generated by MobileGlues during runtime (used to speed up loading) will be cleared.
• Log files: Log files generated during the operation of MobileGlues will be deleted.

Please note, this action is irreversible. Once you click "OK", all the files mentioned above will be permanently deleted and cannot be recovered. If you are going to use MobileGlues again in the future, you will need to reconfigure it.

Are you sure you want to continue?
MobileGlues related files have been completely removed.\nIf you need to completely remove MobileGlues from your device, please uninstall this software.
MobileGlues stores its configuration in the MG folder of your internal storage. Choose how the app may access it:
Direct read/write. You will be taken to the system settings to grant it.
Grant only the MG folder via the system file picker.

The system file picker will open next. In the root of your internal storage, find the MG folder (create it with the picker\'s “New folder” button if it does not exist), open it, then tap “Use this folder”.
That folder is not named “MG”. MobileGlues reads a fixed path (/sdcard/MG), so please pick the MG folder.
Grant storage access to view and modify renderer settings.
This app is free software that runs completely offline. Here is exactly what it touches.

Only the MG folder in your internal storage: config.json (your renderer settings), stats.json (how many times a game has loaded the renderer), glsl_cache.tmp (shader cache) and MobileGlues log files. Nothing outside that folder is read, modified or deleted.

The renderer (a native library inside your game) reads /sdcard/MG directly, so this app needs a way to write the same folder. You choose between “All files access” and granting just the MG folder via the system file picker (SAF), and you can revoke either at any time in system settings.

A few private preferences on your device: UI style, chosen authorization method, the launch count at which sponsorship was last mentioned, and whether you have donated. No personal data, no identifiers.
“GitHub Release” and “Sponsor” open pages in your own browser. Once you leave this app, the destination site is responsible for its own behavior.

This app does not declare the INTERNET permission — check it in system settings or in the package manifest. Uploading anything is therefore technically impossible: there is nothing to leak because nothing can leave the device.
This is your %1$dth launch of MobileGlues. If it has been useful, you may buy the developers a coffee — entirely optional, and nothing is locked either way.
If you happened to complete a donation just now, tap “Donated” and we will never bring this up again. If not, that is completely fine too.
